summary: Router 0.26.1, ADR-0081 (complements ADR-0073). skirnir-router.service gains ReadOnlyPaths=-/etc/skirnir-router/tls next to the certs line: installations set up before router.py --init keep certificate and key in /etc/skirnir-router/tls, which lay inside ReadWritePaths=/etc/skirnir-router, so a compromised router could replace its TLS key and certificate there or plant a symlink for an ACME client that writes in place. Verified first that the router never writes below tls: control_tls is only read (config.unreadable_files with os.access R_OK, app.py load_cert_chain, config.cert_fingerprint for node certificates); every router write targets a fixed file name next to config.yaml (roles.yaml, nodes.json, metrics/usage/perf/ollama-latest JSON, events.jsonl, deletions.jsonl), /var/lib/skirnir-router or /var/log/skirnir-router, or an operator-set log path; router.py --init writes only config.yaml; no code generates certificates; install.sh, deploy.py, the certificate path/service and the secrets units never write there (the certificate is written by the ACME client as root outside the router's mount namespace; the router is restarted by skirnir-router-cert.path). The leading '-' keeps hosts without the folder starting. selftest_privilege_paths now requires both read-only lines with '-', checks that the --init defaults, both example configurations and the watched path of skirnir-router-cert.path are not router-writable under the unit (most specific path setting decides), that the router's own files stay writable, and as the rejected case that the same unit without the tls line leaves certificate and key writable. Threat model EN/DE and register TM-14 controls, install guide EN/DE (TLS section, checklist), CHANGELOG v0.31.1 row.

findings.evidence: router/skirnir-router.service had ReadWritePaths=/etc/skirnir-router and made only /etc/skirnir-router/certs read-only; certificate and key of older installations in /etc/skirnir-router/tls were writable by the router process (uid 0 without capabilities, owner bits suffice). Impact: a compromised router replaces the certificate it presents to nodes and clients persistently, and with an ACME client that writes into the existing file a planted symlink turns renewal into a root write.
findings.resolution: ReadOnlyPaths=-/etc/skirnir-router/tls. Under systemd 259 append, unlink, create and rename in tls are refused while roles.yaml in the parent stays writable; without the line all four are allowed. selftest_privilege_paths fails without the line (3 failures) and without the '-' prefix (2 failures).

findings.evidence: Pre-existing, unchanged in kind: certificate and key in any other folder below /etc/skirnir-router (or /var/lib, /var/log/skirnir-router) stay router-writable; if certs or tls is a symlink, systemd mounts its target read-only but the link is an entry in the router-writable /etc/skirnir-router and can be swapped (confirmed under systemd 259: write through the link refused, replacing the link allowed). Same for certs since ADR-0073.
findings.resolution: Documented in install-router EN/DE (keep certificate and key in certs, tls or outside the writable folders; real folders, not symlinks) and in ADR-0081's consequences. Removed for good by the dedicated router user that TM-14's next action already plans.

tests.command: python test/selftest_privilege_paths.py (Windows; unit, deploy and passthrough checks)
tests.evidence: selftest_privilege_paths: all passed (22 static checks). Counter-checks on a copy of the unit: without ReadOnlyPaths=-/etc/skirnir-router/tls 3 failures (folder line, tls certificate/key writable, rejected case); with the line but without '-' 2 failures.
They skip on Windows; the renderers are unchanged by this PR and CI runs the cases on Linux.

tests.command: systemd-run --user --wait --pipe -p ProtectSystem=strict -p ReadWritePaths=<tmp>/etc -p ReadOnlyPaths=-<tmp>/etc/certs -p ReadOnlyPaths=-<tmp>/etc/tls -p ReadOnlyPaths=-<tmp>/etc/missing ... (WSL Ubuntu, systemd 259, user manager, throwaway tree)
tests.evidence: With the tls line: append/rm/create/rename in tls refused, certs refused, roles.yaml allowed, a missing '-' folder does not stop the start; write through a listed symlink refused, swapping the link allowed. Without the tls line: all tls operations allowed.

tests.command: ruff check .; python router/router.py --check router/config.example.yaml --pure; python test/check_adr_index.py; python test/check_pinned_references.py; python tools/security/lock_requirements.py check; python test/selftest_control_flow.py && python test/check_control_flow.py
tests.evidence: All checks passed; configuration ok: 5 roles, 7 models; ADR index ok: 81 ADRs; pinned references 0 findings; Python locks 0 problems; control flow ok.

tests.command: python test/selftest_threat_review.py, selftest_install.py, selftest_init.py, selftest_english_names.py, selftest_posture.py, selftest_log_hygiene_paths.py, selftest_config_load.py, selftest_trusted_gate.py
tests.evidence: All exit 0 on Windows (selftest_install: OK, 3 skipped as on Windows before).

tests.command: python test/run_tests.py (end-to-end suite, Windows, loopback ports)
tests.evidence: Second run: 0 failures, 332 PASS. The first run had 1 failure, 'Residency: rank-1 prewarmed again after evictor idle' (model loaded, but no residency prewarm event within the test's 12 heartbeat polls); the suite is timing-sensitive and runs nightly in CI for that reason, and this change touches no router logic (unit file and version string).
Public-change scan: 0 finding(s); manual review of the added lines: example paths and synthetic folder names only.

limitations: No production host was inspected; that a deployment keeps its TLS files in /etc/skirnir-router/tls comes from the operator. deploy.py prefers a skirnir-router.service from the operator's ops folder if one exists; such an override needs the same line.

The systemd check ran under the WSL user manager, not as the root system service; there ProtectSystem=strict did not make an unlisted folder under $HOME read-only, so it evidences the precedence of ReadWritePaths/ReadOnlyPaths, not ProtectSystem.

systemd mounts the folder when the router starts: a tls folder created later is read-only from the next restart; a running router keeps an older directory if the whole folder is replaced, until the restart skirnir-router-cert.path triggers.
unit_may_write in the self-test models only ReadWritePaths, ReadOnlyPaths and InaccessiblePaths with the most specific match; StateDirectory/LogsDirectory and symlinks are not modelled.
The router still runs as root; this closes one more writable location, not the root identity (TM-14 stays open).
